The Deep Sea Anglerfish: A Field Guide

The anglerfish is one of the ocean's strangest inhabitants, living at crushing depths where sunlight never reaches. Its bioluminescent lure, dangling from a modified fin ray, draws curious prey close enough to swallow whole, a hunting strategy refined over millions of years of evolution.

Unlike most predators, the female anglerfish grows dramatically larger than the male, who spends much of his short life searching for a mate in total darkness, guided almost entirely by scent, and upon finding one, fuses permanently to her body for the remainder of his existence, becoming little more than a sperm-producing appendage.

Researchers have documented over two hundred species across every ocean basin, from the frigid waters of the Arctic to the warm currents near the equator, each adapted with its own lure shape, coloration, and hunting depth, illustrating just how successful this bizarre body plan has been across evolutionary time.
